description:
## Problem

The Elixir extractor finds System.cmd calls (e.g. in reach/lib/reach/check/changed.ex) but catseye doesn't flag them as CommandInjection. The issue is likely that tainted data flows into System.cmd via string interpolation ("#{base}...HEAD") but the taint engine doesn't track this.

## Evidence

From reach/lib/reach/check/changed.ex:
  defp changed_files(base) do
    case System.cmd("git", ["diff", "--name-only", base <> "...HEAD"], stderr_to_stdout: true) do
  end

The extractor correctly identifies System.cmd at line 56, but catseye doesn't report CommandInjection because:
1.  is a function parameter (potential taint source)
2.  creates a string via interpolation
3. The interpolated string flows into System.cmd's args list
4. The taint engine doesn't track through string interpolation to args

## Expected Behavior

When a function parameter flows into System.cmd args via string concatenation/interpolation, it should be flagged as CommandInjection.

## Suggested Fix

1. Improve Elixir taint propagation to track through <> (string concatenation) and #{} (interpolation)
2. Ensure the Elixir mapper creates proper arg nodes so the taint engine can trace data flow
3. Consider adding "base"-like param names as taint sources when they flow into System.cmd
title: Elixir: taint propagation for System.cmd args via string interpolation
